title: cardinals amid 2006 title celebration open series vs white sox  flm 2026 09 11
text:
September 11 - On pace to finish a second straight season with a losing record, the St. Louis Cardinals plan on leaning into their much more successful past as the Chicago White Sox come to town Friday night to start a three-game set.
The Cardinals will celebrate ​their World Series championship of 2006 on Friday. Albert Pujols, Yadier Molina, Adam Wainwright, Jim Edmonds, Chris Carpenter, ‌manager Tony La Russa and others are scheduled to appear.
A day later, the Cardinals will induct Pujols and Molina into their Hall of Fame. Both perennial All-Stars will become eligible for enshrinement in the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, N.Y., in the class of 2028.
The contemporary Cardinals (72-75) are coming off ​a 4-5 road trip against the Los Angeles Dodgers, Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants. St. Louis has dropped seven ​of 11 overall.
"We did some things well, we did some things that weren't that good -- no different ⁠than any other road trip," said manager Oliver Marmol, whose team is 6 1/2 games outside of a playoff spot with 15 ​games to go.
St. Louis left-hander Matthew Liberatore (5-14, 5.57 ERA) takes the mound in the series opener having dropped six straight starts since Aug. ​8, posting a 7.71 ERA in that span. In his past nine outings, Liberatore is 0-8 with a 6.75 ERA.
Liberatore has 1-0 record and a 2.79 ERA in two career appearances against the White Sox, including a victorious start in June 2025.
The White Sox, another team La Russa used to manage, ​fell to 3-6 in September after getting swept at home by the Pirates. Pittsburgh capped the series with a 2-0 win Thursday ​night. Though the White Sox rank seventh in the majors in runs scored, they put up just five runs in the three-game series.
Chicago's American League ‌Central ⁠lead has shrunk from 5 1/2 games on Aug. 16 to 1 1/2 games over the second-place Cleveland Guardians (74-73). The White Sox (75-71) could earn a first-round bye in the postseason after losing more than 100 games in each of the past three seasons.
"We're still in a good spot as far as energy, the way the guys are showing up to the field, the environment and vibe," White Sox ​manager Will Venable said. "We just ​ran into some tough pitching ⁠and didn't have any answers for it.
"We've got some work to do, to cover some fastballs and start scoring some runs."
Anthony Kay (9-8, 4.47 ERA) is set to start for the White Sox. The left-hander ​will be making his first career start against the Cardinals and his first appearance against them ​in three years. ⁠In three relief outings vs. St. Louis, Kay allowed three runs in 3 1/3 innings.
Like Liberatore, Kay is looking to end a winless streak. He is 0-3 with a 6.84 ERA in his past five appearances.
Kay took a loss against the Minnesota Twins on Saturday. After throwing ⁠three shutout ​innings, he gave up two runs in the fourth, then three more in ​the fifth, exiting after 4 1/3 frames.
"We got in a groove early and then kind of fell apart," Kay said. "... It comes down to execution and maybe some ​pitch-calling that we can work on second time, third time through. They're clearly seeing something that we have to work on."
--Field Level Media
